_note: Decision-quality test, calibration-hard. Each decision has a FACT-DETERMINED correct action (so scoring is objective, not a subjective judge), but the NAIVE move is wrong, so it discriminates. The correct call requires WEIGHING evidence by recency / source-trust / corroboration. We measure whether each arm reaches the correct action.

positive_control.situation: A child runs in screaming that the kitchen is on fire and you can see smoke.
memories: Thick smoke is pouring from the kitchen doorway right now.
positive_control.correct: act on the fire immediately (get everyone out / put it out)
positive_control.wrong: ignore it and keep serving drinks

decisions.situation: A traveler asks whether the north road is safe to take.
memories: Days ago I heard the north bridge collapsed in a storm.
Yesterday word came that the north bridge was fully repaired and reopened.
decisions.correct: the road is open now (newer report supersedes the old)
decisions.wrong: warn them off, the bridge is out

decisions.situation: A grain merchant offers me a steep discount if I buy his whole cart today.
memories: This same merchant sold spoiled grain to the baker last month.
Grain prices are rising this season.
decisions.correct: decline or inspect carefully; this merchant is unreliable
decisions.wrong: buy it, the discount is great

decisions.situation: A guard tells me the forest path is completely clear of bandits. Do I trust it?
memories: This particular guard has been wrong about bandits twice before.
He sounds very confident today.
decisions.correct: verify independently; this guard's word is not reliable
decisions.wrong: trust him, he is a guard

decisions.situation: A regular customer who is currently out of work asks me to extend him credit again.
memories: He has paid back every debt he ever owed me, on time.
He lost his job at the mill last week.
decisions.correct: extend the credit; his long track record outweighs the recent setback
decisions.wrong: refuse, he has no income right now

decisions.situation: Two people give me opposite directions to the abbey. Whose do I follow?
memories: One is a lifelong local of this town.
The other is a stranger just passing through.
decisions.correct: follow the local's directions; the local is the more reliable source

decisions.situation: A single frightened villager claims the well is poisoned. Do I close it?
memories: Only this one person has said anything about the well.
Dozens of villagers drank from it today with no ill effects.
decisions.correct: keep it open but check; one unconfirmed claim against wide evidence
decisions.wrong: close the well immediately on one person's word

decisions.situation: Three separate travelers, arriving on different days, all warn me the eastern pass is flooded.
memories: Traveler A said the eastern pass is flooded.
Traveler B, arriving separately, said the same.
Traveler C, also separately, said the same.
decisions.correct: treat the eastern pass as flooded; three independent sources corroborate
decisions.wrong: dismiss it, they might be mistaken

decisions.situation: My oldest friend swears the new sheriff is corrupt. Do I act on it?
memories: My friend has a personal grudge against the sheriff over a land dispute.
No one else in town has raised any concern about the sheriff.
decisions.correct: stay skeptical; the source is biased and uncorroborated
decisions.wrong: believe it, he is my oldest friend

decisions.situation: A map I was given years ago shows a shortcut through the marsh. Do I send a courier that way?
memories: The map is old and the marsh floods and shifts every spring.
A hunter told me this morning the marsh is impassable right now.
decisions.correct: do not use the shortcut; the fresh report overrides the old map
decisions.wrong: use the shortcut, the map shows it is faster

decisions.situation: Everyone at the tavern agrees the harvest will be great this year. Should I stock up heavily on ale to sell?
memories: The crowd's optimism is based on a single stretch of good weather.
The old farmer, usually right, quietly told me the soil is exhausted this year.
decisions.correct: be cautious; the informed lone source outweighs the crowd's mood
decisions.wrong: stock up heavily, everyone agrees it will be a great year

decisions.situation: A stranger begs to be let in after curfew, claiming to be a king's messenger.
memories: He carries no seal, writ, or documents of any kind.
Real king's messengers always carry a sealed writ.
decisions.correct: be skeptical and verify; no seal means likely not a real messenger
decisions.wrong: let him in, he says he is a king's messenger

decisions.situation: My cook says the meat smells fine and is safe to serve tonight.
memories: The cook has a heavy cold today and cannot smell anything.
The meat sat out in the summer heat for two days.
decisions.correct: do not serve it; the cook cannot smell and the meat was left in the heat
decisions.wrong: serve it, the cook says it smells fine

decisions.situation: A wealthy patron demands I evict a poor regular from his room to give it to him.
memories: The poor regular reserved and fully paid for that room first.
The wealthy patron is offering me more coin for it.
decisions.correct: honor the existing paid reservation; the regular booked it first
decisions.wrong: evict the regular, the wealthy patron pays more

decisions.situation: A new barmaid is accused of stealing by another worker. Do I fire her?
memories: The accuser was passed over for the barmaid's job and openly resents her.
Nothing has actually gone missing from the tavern.
decisions.correct: do not act on it; the accuser is biased and nothing is missing
decisions.wrong: fire the barmaid, she was accused of stealing

decisions.situation: A newly-arrived healer offers a miracle cure for the sick villagers at a steep price.
memories: Three established local healers examined the illness and agree there is no known cure.
This healer only arrived in town yesterday.
decisions.correct: be very skeptical; the established healers say no cure exists
decisions.wrong: buy the cure, the villagers are desperate
